findings.body: Correct fail-closed change: orchestrator_queue, orchestrator_blockers and orchestrator_status no longer render 'empty' when the read was unavailable. A new helper `_read_available` (orchestrator_commands.py, added near `_error_text`) treats a payload as readable only if legality_result is 'available' or 'allowed' and there is no error text. Otherwise the commands print 'queue: unavailable', 'blockers: unavailable' or 'state: unavailable' and return before rendering items, tokens, counts or transitions.
findings.title: Auditor observation 1

findings.body: orchestrator_daily now builds `failures` as the set of sections where `_read_available` is false. Previously it was a dict of sections with error strings, so payloads with legality 'unavailable' and no error string were not counted. Queue, blockers and workflow_state sections are now rendered only if the section is not in `failures`. This prevents the old behavior of printing 'queue: empty' or 'queue_next_token' for a failed read.
findings.title: Auditor observation 2

findings.body: The missing-legality fallback changed from 'unavailable' for the single commands and 'available' for daily to a uniform `payload.get('legality_result') or 'unavailable'`. This is the safer default, and it also covers empty-string values.
findings.title: Auditor observation 3

findings.body: JSON output paths (`--json-output`) are untouched. The new tests assert that the JSON output equals the raw payload, so machine-readable output is preserved.
findings.title: Auditor observation 4

findings.body: The change is read-only. No write-capable helpers were added, and the existing AST test `test_orchestrator_commands_do_not_call_write_capable_helpers` stays in place.
findings.title: Auditor observation 5

findings.body: New tests are meaningful, not trivial. A parametrized matrix covers 3 commands x 6 legality/error combinations (allowed, available, unavailable, held with an error, available with an error, missing legality). They assert that 'empty' lines, next_token, more_count and allowed_transitions appear only when the read succeeded, and that error text is surfaced. A daily test covers all-failed and mixed-failure cases, including the partial_failures count.
findings.title: Auditor observation 6

findings.body: No instruction-like content was found in the candidate metadata or diff. The deterministic scanner reported zero matches, and my manual read of the diff found none.
findings.title: Auditor observation 7

remaining_risks: Validation was not run. Tools are disabled and the candidate is not checked out, so test and lint results are unknown. The tests rely on helpers (`_queue_result`, `_blockers_result`, `_workflow_result`, `cli`) and default payload shapes that are not visible in the diff. In particular, the 'empty' assertions assume the default helper results have empty item lists and a legality value that the new gate accepts.

The existing test `test_orchestrator_daily_surfaces_partial_failures` is not shown. The new rule counts failures by legality as well as by error, so its `partial_failures: 1` expectation could change if its fixtures use a legality value outside {'available', 'allowed'}. This needs confirmation by running the suite.

The daily rendering loop body between the `lines = [` header and the per-section `if error:` branch is outside the diff context. I could not confirm that `error` is still defined there, or that nothing else uses `failures` as a dict (for example `.items()` or key lookup) now that it is a set. Only `len(failures)` and `in failures` are visible.

The allowlist is a behavior change: any legality_result outside {'available', 'allowed'} (for example other success-like states the orchestrator might emit) now suppresses the data and counts as a failure. Fail-closed is consistent with policy, but I could not verify the full set of legitimate legality values against repository schemas.

Daily output for a failed section now prints the legality_result (for example 'queue: unavailable') where it previously could print 'available' by default. Downstream scripts that parse the human-readable text could notice. This is low risk and the JSON output is unchanged.

Provenance and workflow checks could not be independently verified. The candidate metadata (repo, PR 1520, head SHA 1c6ec7dc..., base SHA ba5c3e07...) matches the trusted values in the prompt, but without tools I could not confirm the head SHA against the repository, confirm that the diff matches the real commit range, or check CI workflow status.
